clue.text: Mercy returned by footballer

parts.note: to give quarter is to show mercy to a beaten enemy
a ball returned has come back

explanation.surface: A footballer hands back clemency after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a reversal of a word for mercy, but 'returned' simply supplies its own synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the play-calling position in American football, so its player is a footballer.

clue.text: On a billet after a company has left

indicators.note: the company departing means those letters drop out of the voucher word

parts.note: a billet can be a ticket or voucher, here a coupon
CO is the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Someone is billeted somewhere after their military company has moved on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Billet' suggests soldiers' quarters, but here it is a ticket or voucher.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition is a slightly formal synonym of plain 'on', as in once upon a time.

clue.text: Bank which takes part in a more effective way of saving money

indicators.note: the answer forms part of the following words, sitting across two of them

parts.words: a more effective way of saving money

explanation.surface: A bank promotes itself as a better way to save money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks financial, but it is a ridge of rock or sand in the sea, found spanning 'more effective'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of rock or coral near the sea surface is a bank in the nautical sense.

clue.text: Wager one has turned into an insect

indicators.note: the letters of the bet word plus the numeral are turned into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A gambler's bet has somehow become a creepy-crawly.
explanation.definitionFit: This pincered creature is a common garden insect.

clue.text: Maximum publicity for one who refuses capital to the railways

parts.note: someone who bans, refusing permission, is a banner
a head is the top or capital of something, as a column's capital is its head
railway lines, or simply lines, means the railway tracks

explanation.surface: Someone denies the railway companies their funding, and it makes the front pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money, but here it means the top of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge type across the top of a front page gives a story the most publicity a paper can.

clue.text: Provides food and puts a note into vehicles

indicators.note: the note is placed into the middle of the vehicles word

parts.note: cars are vehicles
te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone delivers meals and leaves a message in the cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests a written message, but it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply food and drink, as at a function, is to do the catering.

clue.text: If the great work were unfinished it might make me practise

annotationWithheld.why: If the great work were unfinished it might make me practise (11): a reverse anagram, MASTERPIEC (the answer less its last E) being an anagram of ME PRACTISE; no clue word supplies the E as a leaf, so the grammar cannot build it without a bare letter
annotationWithheld.clue: If the great work were unfinished it might make me practise

clue.text: A ploughman's in the City?

parts.note: a ploughman pushes the share of his plough; transplanted to the financial City of London he would be a dealer pressing stocks on buyers

explanation.surface: A ploughman's lunch is being eaten in the City.
explanation.walkthrough: A ploughman's is a British pub lunch of bread and cheese, which the surface evokes; the City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodgy dealer who aggressively sells shares to the public is the stock-market counterpart of a ploughman.

clue.text: Clean up the city

definitions.meaning: to wash oneself thoroughly in a tub
a spa city in Somerset, England

explanation.definitionFit: A tub soak cleans you, and the Somerset spa city famous for Roman baths shares the name.

clue.text: Fruit which makes man get a rope twisted

indicators.note: a rope being twisted suggests the letters of these words are wound into a new order

explanation.surface: A fruit somehow drives a man to grab a twisted rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed-filled red fruit with a leathery rind.

clue.text: Light which brings animals back

indicators.note: bringing the creatures back means the word for them is read backwards

parts.note: rats are animals

explanation.surface: A lamp somehow attracts animals back.
explanation.definitionFit: A celestial body shining in the night sky is a light.

clue.text: They follow vehicles when mistakes are made before starting the engine in cars

annotationWithheld.why: They follow vehicles when mistakes are made before starting the engine in cars (11): SLIPS gives 'mistakes', but no reading of 'before starting the engine in cars' yields TREAMS, so the clue as held looks misread or loose
annotationWithheld.clue: They follow vehicles when mistakes are made before starting the engine in cars

clue.text: They indicate letters are missing, upsetting hopers after a delivery

indicators.note: the shuffled hopers come after the delivery in the answer

parts.note: a delivery of mail is the post

indicators.note: upsetting the hopers turns their letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: Hopeful people are let down when the post arrives with letters missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' suggests mail, fitting 'delivery', but in the definition it means characters of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: These punctuation marks stand where characters have been dropped, as in can't.

clue.text: Weapon bring up if the senior officer is missing

annotationWithheld.why: Weapon bring up if the senior officer is missing (4-3): 'bring up' gives REAR and 'if' gives IF, but no reading of 'the senior officer is missing' supplies the M or orders the letters as FIREARM, so the clue as held looks misread
annotationWithheld.clue: Weapon bring up if the senior officer is missing

clue.text: Shady places in which diplomats take their ease

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, the British diplomatic service
to take one's ease is to rest

explanation.surface: Where do diplomats go to relax?
explanation.walkthrough: FO is the Foreign Office, Britain's diplomatic ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodlands of dense trees give plenty of shade.

clue.text: Having tried a wife, I am among the spoilt

indicators.note: the I is placed among the letters of the spoilt word

parts.note: to mar is to spoil, so spoilt is marred

explanation.surface: A man who has tried having a wife finds himself among the spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a wry one: having taken a wife on trial, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who has taken a spouse, put playfully as having given a wife a try.

clue.text: Pet opposite of friend to religion?

indicators.note: each of the two words is turned the opposite way round, each in its own place

parts.note: a pal is a friend
God stands for religion, the object of faith

explanation.surface: Is a pet the opposite of a friend of the church?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one opposite word for the whole phrase; instead each word is turned round separately, and 'religion' stands for its deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pampered dog kept for company is a pet.

clue.text: An official took it easy before the strike

parts.note: to sit back is to take it easy, so took it easy is sat
a rap is a sharp blow or strike

explanation.surface: An official relaxes before a workers' walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action, but it is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A provincial governor of ancient Persia; by extension any petty official.

clue.text: Ineffective member of the team prepares for matches, for they keep people on the rails

definitions.text: they keep people on the rails

parts.note: a team member who contributes nothing is called a passenger
a player trains before matches

explanation.surface: A weak team member gets ready for games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rails' suggests a ship's or a moral rail, but it is the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway services carrying the public keep travellers on the tracks.

clue.text: Immoral women just about ring for their cards

indicators.note: the immoral women go just about the ring, enclosing it

parts.note: tarts is slang for loose women
O is a ring by its shape

explanation.surface: Loose women nearly phone about their fortune-telling cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests a phone call, but it is the letter O by its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune-telling packs of picture cards, the sort such women might use.

clue.text: Tried hard for the floating voters

indicators.note: floating voters are undecided, so their letters float into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone worked hard to win over undecided voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floating voters' is a political phrase, but 'floating' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to try hard; this is its past tense.

clue.text: Potter after the soldiers for what is necessary in time of danger

definitions.text: what is necessary in time of danger

indicators.note: the cue comes after the soldiers in the answer

parts.note: RES is short for reserves, soldiers held back
a cue is the stick a snooker player pots the balls with

explanation.surface: A potter follows the soldiers into danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' suggests someone who makes pots or dawdles; it is the snooker cue, which pots balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving someone from harm is what they need when in peril.

clue.text: Included in a table this cause would appear disloyal

definitions.text: Included in a table this cause would appear disloyal

parts.words: Included in a table this cause would appear disloyal
parts.note: a word for a cause, placed inside the word table, produces a word meaning disloyal

explanation.walkthrough: Put inside TABLE, the answer makes TREASONABLE, meaning disloyal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cause or motive for doing something is its grounds.

clue.text: Played for time when unable to eat any more

definitions.meaning: an archaic sense, as fattened in a stall until full

explanation.definitionFit: Stalling is delaying; a beast fattened in a stall is surfeited, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Observe you include a footnote in return

indicators.note: the whole is then turned round and read backwards
the old word for you takes in the footnote letters

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
PS, postscript, is a note added at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: Note that you add a footnote when replying.
explanation.walkthrough: YE is an old form of 'you' and PS a postscript; the container is formed first and only then is the whole turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of something is to observe it.

clue.text: Food which makes one complain

explanation.definitionFit: Cattle meat is food, and to grumble is to beef about something.

clue.text: Painful feature of last year's epidemic

indicators.note: the answer is part of the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: Last year's epidemic had a painful symptom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'epidemic' suggests an illness, which fits, but the answer sits across 'last year's'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the eyelid is a sore feature of the face.

clue.text: The people who claim to know are wrongly cooing about the aroma

definitions.text: The people who claim to know

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about the aroma word, enclosing it
cooing done wrongly means its letters are put into another order

parts.note: a scent is an aroma

explanation.surface: Self-styled experts coo foolishly over a fragrance.
explanation.walkthrough: The aroma sits inside the shuffled cooing letters just before their final I, not at either end.
explanation.definitionFit: Connoisseurs or experts, people regarded as being in the know.

clue.text: Bearing of one surrounded by human beings

indicators.note: the numeral is placed inside the word for people

parts.note: men means people generally
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A person's manner when in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's look or manner is their bearing.

clue.text: Just as Cupid was love

parts.note: Cupid is the god of love, love given human form

explanation.definitionFit: Embodied, in the way a god stands for an abstract quality like desire.
